newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran labels German trial witness embezzler.
newsitem.headline: Iran labels German trial witness embezzler.

text.p: Iran on Friday denounced as an embezzler and wife-beater an Iranian whose court testimony led a prosecutor to accuse Tehran's leaders of ordering politicial killings in Germany, the official news agency IRNA said.

It said the Iranian Foreign Ministry sent a letter to the German Foreign Ministry naming the Berlin trial witness, identified in Germany only as "Source C". It said he was wanted in Iran on a variety of criminal charges, including embezzlement and cheque fraud.
The agency said the witness embezzled up to $1.8 million from an employee cooperative at an Iranian steel plant, wrote dud cheques for $1 million and once beat his wife, breaking her elbow.
"Source C" gave testimony at the trial of an Iranian and four Lebanese charged with the 1992 murder of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator at a Berlin restaurant.
Partly basing himself on the testimony, a German prosecutor has accused Iranian leaders of having ordered the shootings. Iran has denied involvement in the killings.
A senior Iranian cleric said on Friday Iranians would not tolerate the accusation that Tehran leaders had ordered the killings.

"The (Iranian) people are ready to see themselves wounded and shot at but they are not ready to tolerate any insult to their sanctities," Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast live on state-run Tehran radio.

The IRNA report quoted the letter as saying the witness had been employed by an Iranian embassy in 1983 "with the help of a (foreign) spying service" and later unsuccessfully tried to join the information (internal security) ministry and the foreign ministry.

It was not clear if the letter was part of a large dossier compiled by the Iranian Foreign Ministry on "Source C" that a German prosecutor said on Thursday could delay the end of the Berlin trial which has damaged ties between Tehran and Bonn.
The letter said said Mesbahi later had been arrested briefly for contacts with "dubious foreign personalities" and later "was prevented from continuing contacts with political circles."

Deposed Iranian ex-president Abolhassan Banisar, who also gave testimony at the trial, said "Source C" was a high-level defector who "had direct access to information about (Iranian secret service) operations."
